title: Observability Prism — MVP scope reduction & fallback policy for dashboards, tracing, and cost explorer
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: This ticket captures the decision, rationales, and acceptance criteria for a targeted MVP cut to the Console observability surface. The goal is to ship a minimal, useful set of dashboard cards, a lightweight tracing surface, and a constrained cost explorer while meeting latency and cost SLOs for the hosted product. This is a scope reduction exercise: prioritize developer/engineer use-cases (route triage, cost regressions, and quick root cause signals) and defer lower-value, high-effort features.
background: PM + Eng review on 2025-02-10 highlighted that the original scope for Console observability (full per-request flamegraphs, 30-day trace retention, per-token heatmaps, and dynamic route sampling policies) exceeds delivery budget and risks delaying GA. We must reduce scope to a coherent MVP that supports oncall debugging and basic cost-for-route analysis, and define fallback policies so degraded mode remains useful.
scope_included: Six curated dashboard cards: overall traffic, p50/p95 latency, error rate, tokens-per-request distribution (bucketed), top-10 routes by spend, recent rollout anomalies (alerts feed)
Lightweight tracing: 1-in-N sampling (configurable), request ID correlation, and single-span waterfall view that surfaces service, model variant, and token counts
Cost explorer (MVP): top-10 routes with normalized token cost, delta vs. baseline, and per-route approximate unit cost; exportable CSV of top routes
Rollout / fallback policy: automatic fallback to lower-fidelity cost cards when telemetry is missing and route-level degraded indicators
Minimal telemetry contracts and feature flags to toggle full surfaces for enterprise/private deployments
scope_removed: Per-request flamegraphs and full span-level breakdowns (defer to post-MVP)
30-day hot-trace retention and long-tail indexing (MVP retention capped at 7 days)
Per-token heatmap visualizations and token-by-token cost animation
Custom ad-hoc query builder for traces/dashboards (defer; provide presets only)
Deep statistical anomaly detection and ML-driven cost root-cause (post-MVP)
Full export connector set (only CSV export for top routes in MVP)
High-cardinality route tag analytics (limit cardinality to route + model variant)
Advanced sampling policies (defer dynamic trace sampling; support static sampling rate config)
tradeoffs_and_rationale: Flamegraphs and span-level detail provide high fidelity but are expensive to index and store; deferring reduces infra cost and shortens delivery.
7-day retention preserves useful triage window while keeping storage/costs bounded for GA.
Limiting dashboard cards forces prioritization on the most actionable signals for oncall and product leads.
Static sampling is simpler to implement and easier to validate end-to-end; dynamic sampling will be re-evaluated after MVP usage signals.
Enterprise/private customers can opt into extended retention and deeper traces via dedicated capacity plans later.
We prefer shipping consistently performing, lightweight surfaces over delivering a partially complete heavy-feature set.
Acceptance criteria focus on usefulness for debugging and cost transparency, not exhaustive analytics.
Telemetry contract changes will be backwards compatible where possible; any breaking changes require a coordinated rollout with SDKs/agents.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: 6 live cards available in Console for all hosted customers, showing accurate metrics (traffic, p50/p95, error rate, tokens distribution, top-10 spend routes, rollout anomalies).
Tracing: a sampled trace can be retrieved for a request within 3 seconds of query and shows request id, model variant, and token counts in the single-span waterfall view.
Cost Explorer: top-10 routes by spend are computed and visible, with per-route normalized cost and delta vs baseline for the last 24h.

Performance: enabling the MVP observability surface increases median API latency by <3% and adds no more than X MB memory overhead per serving node under typical load (eng to replace X with measured target during implementation).
Retention: telemetry retention configured to 7 days for synthesized logs/traces; retention behavior documented in Console settings.
Fallback: when detailed telemetry is missing, Console must show a graceful degraded state card with guidance and a link to the fallback diagnostic checklist.
QA: cross-team acceptance tests exist that validate end-to-end metric correctness (unit tests + integration smoke tests + dashboard visual diff on staging).
Docs: short-runbook and 'what changed' notice published in Console help explaining cuts and upgrade path to full observability features.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout in three phases: internal dogfood -> small customer cohort (beta) -> general availability.
Beta cohort selection prioritizes high-usage hosted accounts and current dedicated customers who requested observability early.
Monitor telemetry SLA and error budgets during beta for 2 weeks before GA decision.
Gate GA on acceptance criteria above and a post-beta performance regression < 5% on critical p95 latency for inference endpoints.
Provide toggles for enterprise/private to enable extended retention and deeper traces post-GA.
implementation_notes: Eng to implement static sampling with a single configurable sampling rate exposed in Console and default 1-in-100 for MVP.
Dashboard cards should be driven by aggregated metrics in metrics pipeline (avoid per-request heavy joins in the MVP path).
Cost mapping requires consistent route naming; add a pre-deploy validation step to flag high-cardinality routes.
Console UI components should be built from shared primitives so future re-expansion of cards is straightforward.
Define telemetry contract change PR with SDK and server teams; mark incompatible fields with migration notes.
decisions: Adopt 7-day retention as default for hosted MVP (decision owner: Marcus Lee).
Defer flamegraphs and high-cardinality analytics to post-MVP (decision owner: Aisha Kapoor).
Expose a single sampling rate config for MVP instead of dynamic sampling (decision owner: Eng Lead).
Limit cost explorer export to CSV for top routes in MVP; full export connectors deferred to later.
follow_up_tasks: PM to publish 'what changed' doc and customer upgrade path by 2025-03-01.
Eng to submit telemetry contract PR and compatibility tests by 2025-02-20.
Design to produce final MVP card visuals and small-screen behavior by 2025-02-24.
SRE to run load tests with observability surface enabled and publish results to PR by 2025-03-05.
Support to prepare routing/diagnostic checklist for degraded mode and link into Console help.
notes: This ticket replaces earlier broader scope items — it should be used as the canonical source for MVP acceptance criteria.
We expect to iterate quickly on retention and sampling after initial usage data; prioritize telemetry that enables these iterations.
If customer feedback indicates critical missing signals, we will consider surgical re-additions rather than wholesale scope expansion.
